newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia upbeat on Bulgaria trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia upbeat on Bulgaria trade agreement.

text.p: Slovenia said on Friday it expected trade with Bulgaria to increase significantly when a free trade agreement between the two nations comes into force in January next year.
The agreement, to be signed in Sofia today, will gradually reduce duties on industrial goods to zero by the year 2000.
"From January 1997 custom tariffs on about 35 percent of all industrial goods will be abolished," a spokeswoman at the ministry of economic relations and development told Reuters.
Slovenian exports to Bulgaria mainly consist of cars, drugs, chemicals and aluminium products. Imports include oil products, wood products, vegetables and copper.
In the first nine months of this year, exports to Bulgaria were worth $6.8 million, a 30 percent drop on the same period of 1995. Imports slumped by 86.7 percent to $2.88 million.
The ministry said the falls were mainly a result of economic difficulties in Bulgaria.
In 1995 trade with Bulgaria represented 0.2 percent of Slovenia's foreign trade.
